Q1: Poly(lactide)'s hazard profile is largely data deficient across several categories, including carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards (CMR), environmental hazards (ENV), endocrine disruption (EDC), inhalation (IHL), oral (ORL), and organ/systemic hazards (OGN), all rated Tier 4. However, for dermal and eye hazards (SKN), it is rated Tier 2, suggesting potential concerns identified from an expanded scientific perspective beyond official GHS classifications. This indicates a need for further research to fully understand its safety profile.
Q2: Poly(lactide) is not currently identified on any established "Lists of Concern." This absence, coupled with its predominantly data-deficient Tier 4 classifications for most hazard categories, may indicate a lack of comprehensive study rather than a confirmed lack of hazard.
Q3: Despite being extensively studied with 21,000 literature references and having a well-defined chemical structure, Poly(lactide)'s hazard profile remains largely incomplete. Six out of its seven hazard classes are rated Tier 4 (data deficient), indicating a significant lack of comprehensive hazard characterization.
